subject: Critical Thinking
title: Decision Hygiene: Structuring Choice to Reduce Bias
description: A micro-lesson that makes Decision Hygiene: Structuring Choice to Reduce Bias usable.

hook.text: Kahneman's final book argued: don't try to fix biased people. Fix the decision process instead.

buildup.text: 'Decision hygiene' — structured processes that reduce bias without requiring anyone to be aware of their own biases.

discovery.text: Examples: independent judgments before discussion, checklists before decisions, blind evaluations for hiring.

twist.text: Structured interviews predict job performance 2x better than unstructured ones — solely because they reduce bias.

climax.text: The best debiasing doesn't fight human nature. It designs around it.

punchline.text: Don't fix the thinker. Fix the thinking environment.

quiz.question: What is 'decision hygiene' according to Kahneman?
options: Structured processes that reduce bias without requiring self-awareness

details.summary: Decision hygiene uses structured processes to reduce noise and bias in decisions. Like hand-washing prevents infection, decision hygiene prevents contamination of judgment through checklists, blind evaluation, and independent assessment.
details.whyItMatters: Individual debiasing has limits, but structural changes to how decisions are made can systematically reduce bias across entire organizations.
takeaways: Structured processes reduce bias more reliably than awareness alone
Independent assessments before discussion prevent anchoring
Checklists and scoring rubrics standardize evaluation

faq.question: What are specific examples of decision hygiene practices?
faq.answer: Having interviewers score candidates independently before discussing, using structured interview questions, aggregating multiple assessments statistically, and delaying intuitive judgments until after systematic analysis.

faq.question: How does decision hygiene differ from individual debiasing efforts?
faq.answer: Individual debiasing tries to fix thinking person by person. Decision hygiene redesigns the process itself so that biases have less opportunity to operate, regardless of individual awareness or effort.
